_comment: v2 selection (2026-09-07): candidates ranked by rank_exemplars.py over the 727-figure corpus, human-reviewed (exemplar-review/decisions.json: drops + stars), notes written by 4 review agents after viewing each figure. Slots the note-writer judged a misfit were reassigned by hand to the template the reason names (review="reassigned-from-<t>"); a slot was dropped only when the figure already sat under that better template or the reviewer had dropped it there. The same id may appear under several templates; star = must-see.

source.filter: index row type=='diagram' and subtype=='architecture' (272 of 275 records)

exemplars.why_chosen: Cleanest top-down pipeline: colour-coded stage bands, a paper-section gutter on the left, one feedback arrow on the right.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Put a narrow left gutter with section numbers (Sec 3, 4.1, 4.2, 4.3) beside the stage column and route the feedback arrow up the opposite margin so it never crosses the main path.

exemplars.why_chosen: A six-component top-down pipeline that illustrates a mechanism (prefix coalescing) rather than a whole system.
exemplars.what_to_learn: A dashed box around the one step that changed is the cheapest way to say 'this is the optimisation' inside an otherwise ordinary queue-worker-commit pipeline.

exemplars.why_chosen: The smallest complete pipeline in the corpus (6 components, 4 flows, high confidence, 0 weaknesses) at exactly single-column width.
exemplars.what_to_learn: A two-stage pipeline needs only a controller, two stage groups and one labelled hand-off arrow; stacked/offset boxes stand in for 'a pool of N identical instances' without drawing N of them.

exemplars.why_chosen: Vertical five-stage pipeline that pairs every stage with a thumbnail of the artefact it produces; legend on the right.
exemplars.what_to_learn: An output-artefact column beside the stage column turns abstract stage names into concrete data structures without any extra prose.

exemplars.why_chosen: The most extreme banner aspect among clean pipelines (5.57 at 485x87 pt) - the shape a double-column strip pipeline actually takes.
exemplars.what_to_learn: At aspect >5 every stage must be one box-and-caption tall; wrap only the paper's contribution (here DACO) in a dashed group so the eye finds it in a long strip.

exemplars.why_chosen: Three named phases separated by dashed vertical rules, with phase headers set above the band.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Dashed vertical rules plus bold phase headers are enough to segment a pipeline; the same component may legitimately reappear per phase if the headers disambiguate it.

exemplars.why_chosen: Near-monochrome tikz pipeline (1 hue, gray_frac 0.0) whose dashed callouts expand two engines into their replicated cores.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Dashed leader lines mean containment/zoom, solid arrows mean data flow; keeping the two line styles disjoint lets one figure carry both relations.

exemplars.why_chosen: Offline-phase box stacked over an online-phase box with circled numbers 1-4 driving only the online loop.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Split one-time setup from the per-iteration loop with a dashed group boundary, and number only the steps that repeat.

exemplars.why_chosen: Double-column pipeline (aspect 4.0) with an inside legend and a mirrored encoder/decoder around a transmitted artefact.
exemplars.what_to_learn: At double column, mirror the two halves around the one object that crosses between them, and park a two-entry legend in the empty top strip.

exemplars.why_chosen: A starred, high-confidence core pipeline exemplar: a depth-3 dashed Solver group nests two title-bar stages (Sequence Blaster, Parallelism Planner) before handing off to a separate solid Executor box, in 7 components and 4 flows.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Use a dashed box to group a multi-stage sub-pipeline as one unit distinct from the solid downstream stage, append section references directly onto stage titles, and use small coloured-bar card icons to encode variable-length data instead of prose.

exemplars.why_chosen: High-confidence pipeline with 5 circled step markers and a dashed zoom callout that expands one stage into 3 sub-steps, rendered in an icon-illustrated style rather than plain boxes.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Circle-number every step in traversal order even across a callout boundary (1 outside, 2-4 inside, 5 outside); hang the callout as a dashed-border box off the stage it details, and use one colour per role (active vs passive) instead of a legend.

exemplars.why_chosen: Double-column pipeline with 5 stages labelled by their section numbers (5.1-5.5), each its own boxed sub-diagram, and a big return arrow at the bottom literally closing the loop, in 6 components and 6 flows.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Number stages with the section numbers already used in the prose instead of plain digits, so panels map straight to text, and keep one consistent colour per semantic role across every panel (blue=ambiguous, yellow=candidate, green/red=accept/reject) instead of a legend.

exemplars.why_chosen: A clean floor-level pipeline exemplar: 9 plain blue-outlined stage boxes in one strict left-right row from App Containers to Wire, with gray funnel icons marking the two places where per-core queues fan in.
exemplars.what_to_learn: When the point is just that packets pass through these layers in order, skip numbering and legends entirely, and reuse one small funnel or trapezoid glyph wherever parallel per-core resources converge instead of drawing every core's queue.

exemplars.why_chosen: High-confidence top-down pipeline for the fan-out/fan-in variant: 4 identical uniformly-styled boxes inside one outer container fan out from a single input and reconverge at a Concatenate stage, in only 5 components.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Give parallel same-role branches identical fill and shape so the eye reads them as one repeated unit, and reserve differently coloured dashed lines for the routing step, keeping solid black arrows for the shared input split and final concatenation.

exemplars.why_chosen: High-confidence pipeline with a below-figure legend, one of only 19% of pipelines that legend, explaining that every green full-precision layer is paired with a pink STE band, across 11 components and 12 flows.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Pair each functional layer box with a thin coloured band directly beneath it to show a per-layer transform without extra boxes, route the one recurrent connection as a curved dashed arrow into a distinctly coloured memory block, and define the colour code in a legend below the figure.

exemplars.why_chosen: High-confidence double-column pipeline in the phase-divided variant: a dashed horizontal rule splits the canvas into a Policy-Authoring band and an Implementing/Monitoring band, while three circled numbers trace the green process boxes across both.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Use a single dashed rule across the whole canvas to separate two operational phases instead of drawing two boxes, keep the numbered main-path boxes one colour against plain icon inputs, and label each phase in coloured text at the rule itself.

exemplars.why_chosen: High-confidence pipeline in the zoom-into-lanes variant: a short top row of alternating Dense/MoE boxes expands into 3 parallel GPU lanes, with the two AlltoAllv arrows recoloured red to flag the operation under study.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Zoom a single stage of a short top-level chain into a lower panel of repeated per-worker lanes to show what happens inside one step, and recolour only the specific operation under study in the accent colour, leaving the rest gray or blue.

exemplars.why_chosen: Star exemplar of the pipeline-plus-aligned-timeline variant: a two-phase checkpoint pipeline (GPU-to-CPU snapshot, CPU-to-storage persist) sits directly above a synchronized train/checkpoint timeline that red-flags the one stall case.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Stack a structural diagram directly over a time axis sharing its horizontal alignment, so a highlighted timeline event reads as a direct consequence of the boxes above it; reserve red for the one failure case and use dashed brackets to group timeline phases.

exemplars.why_chosen: A floor-sized pipeline, 4 components and 3 flows, pairing a compact cache-in-front-of-tree diagram with a results-callout panel; the record itself flags this mixing of architecture and results as a weakness.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Keep the architecture path itself tiny and legible, batch to cache table to evicted-and-reordered write to tree, using just two colours for the two paths; avoid this figure's flaw of parking results text beside the diagram instead of encoding it in the diagram.

exemplars.why_chosen: Star, high-confidence double-column pipeline with 7 circled numbered stages along the main line and matching dashed callouts hanging below expanding four of them, ending in a small rendered heatmap thumbnail.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Keep the numbered main path as one row of plain boxes and drop expanded explanation into dashed callout boxes underneath, tied by leader lines and annotation text back to the numbered step they detail; finish a signal-processing pipeline with a rendered-output thumbnail, not just a label.

exemplars.why_chosen: High-confidence pipeline with two nested feedback loops, a fast orientation-search loop on the left and a slower backend-retraining loop on the right, linked by one hand-off point, across 8 components and 8 flows.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Draw a fast inner loop and a slower outer loop as two visually distinct cycles joined at one hand-off point; the record's weakness notes that unboxed colour-square groups only work if proximity alone can carry their scope, so box small repeated icon groups instead of relying on adjacency.

exemplars.why_chosen: High-confidence, dense pipeline exemplar with 25 components, near the template's upper range, that abandons a single line for a five-box numbered grid, each nested with its own sub-pipeline, plus one gray loop arrow.
exemplars.what_to_learn: When a pipeline is really a whole-lifecycle map, arrange the numbered stages in a compact grid rather than one long row, nest each stage's own sub-steps inside it, and draw a periodic feedback relationship as one separate curved arrow in a second colour rather than reusing the numbered arrows.

exemplars.why_chosen: High-confidence pipeline nesting five numbered sub-stages inside just two top-level hardware containers, using a worked example highlighted in blue and threaded through the boxes to make an abstract packet pipeline concrete.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Nest a fine-grained numbered sequence inside two or three coarse top-level containers rather than one box per step, highlight one concrete instance in an accent colour as it moves through every stage, and drop dashed leaders from bottom annotations up to the exact stage that consumes each field.

exemplars.why_chosen: High-confidence double-column pipeline with 15 flows, near the template's high end, that nests a fourth numbered stage into a much larger sub-pipeline box, ending in a highlighted test case and a check/cross verdict.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Let the last numbered stage expand into its own multi-step boxed sub-pipeline with its own internal feedback loop rather than forcing every step to the same size, and close a two-execution comparison with a check/cross icon pair; the record's weakness warns to add a legend once icons and dashed groups get this dense.

exemplars.why_chosen: Star, high-confidence pipeline flanked by labelled Input and Output panels, with a dotted Perspect boundary separating the paper's own compute-filter-refine loop from off-the-shelf tools attached above and below the main line.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Bookend a pipeline with explicit Input/Output panels rather than bare arrows at the edges, attach third-party tool names as small boxes above or below the stage they instrument instead of putting them on the main line, and mark the contribution with a dotted boundary plus one internal feedback arrow.

exemplars.why_chosen: High-confidence pipeline in the fan-out/fan-in variant: a trapezoid connector splits Metadata across 16 identical Pipe Manager boxes elided with a vertical ellipsis, while a separate lower lane carries bulk Data to the same DMA Engine.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Use trapezoid connectors, not sixteen arrows, to fan data to and from N identical replicated boxes, elide the middle instances with a vertical ellipsis, and keep the bulk-data lane physically separate from the control lane; draw side-channel control inputs thinner so they are not mistaken for the main dataflow.

exemplars.why_chosen: Numbered layered stack where a dashed orange box marks exactly which sub-tree is the paper's contribution.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Wrap the contribution in a dashed accent-coloured box inside the stack, and use paired up/down arrows to show a config-down / telemetry-up interface in one place.

exemplars.why_chosen: Textbook three-tier stack in tikz: outer tier containers, inner module rows, and a dashed line naming a trust/network boundary.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Name tiers in the left margin, keep every module row the same height, and use a single dashed horizontal rule (labelled 'Internet') for the boundary that matters.

exemplars.why_chosen: Flattest layered figure in the set (nesting_depth 1) - three labelled bands, white/gray fills only, circled numbers 1-5 tracing one request.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Colour is optional: white boxes for the traced path and gray for background components, plus dashed band separators, already carry a full layered architecture.

exemplars.why_chosen: One of only 3 double-column layered figures in the corpus; a shared DRAM bus at the top feeds parallel engines below, tagged A-I.
exemplars.what_to_learn: At double column a layered hardware figure becomes bus-on-top with engines hanging below; lettered callouts (A-I) index the prose instead of ordering a flow.

exemplars.why_chosen: Tall single-column layered figure (aspect 0.78) with three tinted bands labelled in a right-hand gutter.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Band labels can live in a rotated right gutter instead of the left, freeing the left margin for the feedback arrow that closes the loop.

exemplars.why_chosen: Nesting depth 3 with a dashed geographic boundary (Region A / Region B) and circled numbers on the request path.
exemplars.what_to_learn: A dashed labelled rule can express a deployment boundary (region, host, trust domain) inside an otherwise ordinary layered stack.

exemplars.why_chosen: Control-plane band on top, a homogeneous GPU row in the middle, one shared resource band at the bottom, split by a dashed rule.
exemplars.what_to_learn: The 'manager over devices over shared pool' sandwich: a dashed horizontal rule separates control plane from data plane and the shared pool is a full-width band.

exemplars.why_chosen: The tallest clean layered figure (aspect 0.67) with explicit 'Layer 1..4' headers, section references and an icon column.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Numbering the layers in their headers and citing sections (SS3.1-SS3.4) makes a very tall single-column stack navigable; each layer gets an icon on the left and its content on the right.

exemplars.why_chosen: Star, high-confidence layered exemplar with tier names in a right-hand gutter (Application, Kernel-space, I/O devices) across 4 dashed-divided bands, and white-vs-gray boxes distinguishing ZRAID's functional logic from its in-memory state, in 13 components.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Put tier labels in a slim right gutter instead of inside the band, use two flat fills, white for logic and gray for state, to separate function from data within one tier, and draw the repeated bottom-tier devices once in full detail then abbreviate the rest to a label only.

exemplars.why_chosen: Star, high-confidence layered exemplar spanning a cluster level above a node level, with each of three contributed modules marked by its own dashed, section-numbered box inside an otherwise standard Kubernetes layout, at nesting depth 3.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Use one dashed box per contribution, each carrying its own section number, scattered across whichever tier it actually belongs to, rather than one big accent region; keep a solid-versus-dotted line legend so control paths and data paths stay distinguishable across the whole cluster-to-hardware stack.

exemplars.why_chosen: Star, high-confidence three-layer stack where each band is boxed in its own accent colour and explicitly named, with the dashed dividers themselves labelled as named interfaces and a bottom legend defining solid-versus-dashed line meaning.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Name the dashed boundary line itself instead of leaving it a bare rule, give each of the 3-4 tiers its own accent colour tied to the tier's own name, and put a small solid/dashed legend below the figure when line style carries a data-versus-control meaning.

exemplars.why_chosen: Star, high-confidence layered exemplar of the mirrored-replica variant: identical Graph Store Server and Worker Machine boxes sit side by side at each bottom tier, cross-linked by explicit arrows, in 7 components and 6 flows.
exemplars.what_to_learn: When a tier is really N replicated nodes, draw exactly two identical side-by-side boxes with a crossing arrow between them to stand for the whole replicated set, and reuse the same internal layout one tier below so the eye maps server-to-worker pairs straight down the page.

exemplars.why_chosen: Star, high-confidence layered exemplar with only 6 components and 3 flows: two redundant orange Coordinators cross-connect to two dashed Worker Node containers, each expanded into a scheduler-executor-store stack, over one shared durable store.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Draw redundant top-tier controllers with crossing arrows into every replica below to show any-to-any reachability without extra edges, give every role one flat colour so the internal stack reads at a glance, and let a single full-width bottom box stand for the one shared backing store beneath repeated node containers.

exemplars.why_chosen: Star, high-confidence layered exemplar of the parallel-backend variant: three colour-coded backend boxes sit side by side over one shared dashed core-state box, sandwiched between labelled Control-point and System-call arrows, across 13 components.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Split a middle tier into parallel same-size backend boxes, each its own colour, all resting on one shared dashed core box beneath them, and label the two interception arrows above and below that middle tier by name instead of leaving them bare, making the tier's two boundaries explicit.

exemplars.why_chosen: Star, high-confidence layered exemplar arranged as two side-by-side columns rather than pure horizontal bands, with an orange highlight isolating the shared narrow-waist controllers and circled numbers 1-5 tracing the critical scale-out path through both columns.
exemplars.what_to_learn: When two parallel software stacks share one critical sub-path, draw them as two columns and recolour only the shared boxes that carry the argument, then number the request path across both columns so the highlighted path reads as one continuous route rather than two separate stacks.

exemplars.why_chosen: High-confidence double-column layered exemplar, rare in this template, using 3 side-by-side panels of the identical VM-hypervisor-SmartNIC-disk stack to compare where the critical path sits, with a right-side legend for three arrow styles.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Repeat the exact same small vertical stack across 2-3 panels and vary only which layer is bypassed or duplicated, so the comparison is about position in the stack, not shape; put a shared arrow-style legend to the right when line style, not colour, distinguishes read/write, consistency and copy traffic.

exemplars.why_chosen: Star, high-confidence layered exemplar embedding a literal data-table object as one box and annotating command-line invocations on the flow arrows, split by one rule into a user-space band above and a kernel-space band below.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Draw a tier's artifact as a literal table, columns and all, rather than a plain box when the paper's contribution is the schema itself, and write command strings right on the arrow that triggers them; keep matching colour bands consistent between the table and the running-kernel bar they describe.

exemplars.why_chosen: Star, high-confidence layered exemplar in monochrome grayscale, using only shading depth, not colour, to distinguish the Master Node band from the nested Worker Node band, across 15 components at nesting depth 3.
exemplars.what_to_learn: When colour is not carrying meaning, differentiate nested tiers by shading depth alone, darker gray for the outer container and lighter for inner boxes, and place matched request/response queue icons flanking the control boxes they feed so the master-to-worker path stays readable in one grayscale palette.

exemplars.why_chosen: Star, high-confidence layered exemplar that annotates a numbered request path, steps 1-9, onto a vertical stack from user-space app boxes down to the DFS, with red hit/miss labels at the one decision point.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Overlay circled step numbers straight onto the tier-to-tier arrows of a vertical stack to narrate one concrete request, split a single decision into two coloured branch labels rather than separate diagrams, and use hatching to mark which address ranges are currently backed by a cache block.

exemplars.why_chosen: High-confidence layered background exemplar at floor size, 8 components and 3 flows, stacking host, PCIe band, hardware package and network fabric tiers, with one labelled DMA arrow crossing the boundary.
exemplars.what_to_learn: For a hardware-background figure, draw the bus itself as a distinct shaded band between tiers rather than an arrow, and add only the one cross-boundary arrow the text actually needs instead of wiring every block to every other block.

exemplars.why_chosen: Star, high-confidence two-tier layered exemplar, a blue Server box over an orange Client box over a GPU row, where circled numbers 1-5 on the connecting arrows trace a profiling-optimization-schedule-feedback loop around an embedded lookup-table object.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Embed a small data object, such as a lookup table with one highlighted row, inside the tier that owns it rather than describing it in prose, and number the back-and-forth arrows between just two tiers in interaction order even when several arrows point the same direction, so the loop reads sequentially.

exemplars.why_chosen: Star, high-confidence layered exemplar split top-down into Offline and Online Phase bands, ending in a row of Executor boxes where one is picked out with a red dashed outline as the failure recovered from.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Separate offline planning from online execution as two stacked full-width bands joined by one labelled arrow, draw the bottom tier as a row of otherwise identical worker boxes, and mark the one instance that misbehaves with a red dashed outline instead of a caption.

exemplars.why_chosen: Star, high-confidence baseline layered exemplar with a named dashed API boundary separating an apps-side gutter label from a cloud-side gutter label, and a horizontally repeated Proxy 1...Proxy n sub-box standing for a stateless replica pool.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Label the two sides of a dashed interface line with a short margin tag rather than titling each box separately, and draw a replicated stateless pool as one small sub-box holding numbered instances plus an ellipsis rather than drawing every replica full size.

exemplars.why_chosen: Star, high-confidence layered exemplar where one shared first-level allocator-evictor pair sits above two parallel colour-coded second-level allocator columns, the whole memory manager boxed in one dashed rounded container beneath a plain scheduler-to-workers request line.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Give a shared upper stage one neutral colour pair and let it feed two side-by-side lower columns that each keep their own colour for the rest of the figure, down to the small square page icons at the very bottom, so colour alone tracks which allocator produced which output.

exemplars.why_chosen: Star, medium-confidence layered exemplar of the rare bottom-up direction, stacking a Transformer block from Input Token through self-attention into a Mixture-of-Experts block whose router fans dashed arrows to every expert but bolds the taken path.
exemplars.what_to_learn: When the tiers are literally computation layers of one repeated block, read them bottom-up with input at the floor and output at the ceiling, show repetition with a few offset background rectangles rather than N boxes, and distinguish a router's considered-but-not-taken paths, dashed, from its actual path, bold solid, in one colour.

exemplars.why_chosen: High-confidence layered exemplar of a stepwise zoom: 16 replicated Sorting Cores collapse into one expanded core, linked by a dashed containment line to a further-expanded, blue-highlighted unit below, across 2 panels and nesting depth 3.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Chain two successive zoom-ins top to bottom, engine to one core to one sub-unit, using dashed connector lines to mean containment rather than dataflow, and highlight only the final, most novel block in accent colour; the record's own weakness warns to label small symbols like a comparator explicitly instead of relying on convention.

exemplars.why_chosen: Star, high-confidence two-tier layered exemplar, a purple DRAM band over a green FLASH band, with small coloured grid cells standing for individual sets, and explicit flush and extract-combine arrows crossing the boundary both ways.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Colour the two memory tiers, not just their contents, so DRAM versus flash is legible before reading labels, and represent a pool of same-role objects as a row of small identical boxes; the record flags thin curved feedback arrows as easy to miss, so make a feedback path as heavy as the path it answers.

exemplars.why_chosen: Star, high-confidence layered exemplar with an explicit three-row colour legend inside the frame tying 14 components to three roles, feeding from operator and developer inputs through a planning tier into a jointly labelled hardware-plus-runtime tier.
exemplars.what_to_learn: When more than two colours carry role meaning, put a compact legend inside a free corner rather than relying on labels alone, and let one hardware box be jointly annotated by two different functional tiers, a long-term planner's output above and a short-term runtime's control below, to show both act on the same resource.

exemplars.why_chosen: High-confidence, dense layered exemplar that partitions the whole architecture into three separately dashed-bordered quadrants rather than horizontal bands, colour-coding each quadrant's own role boxes across 15 components and 12 flows.
exemplars.what_to_learn: When a system's levels are conceptual rather than physically stacked, arrange them as separate dashed-bordered quadrants labelled by level name instead of forcing strict top-down bands, and show a before/after transition as two small boxes joined by one arrow inside its own quadrant.

exemplars.why_chosen: Two lettered panels with one shared legend placed below and spanning both.
exemplars.what_to_learn: When both panels use the same colour encoding, the legend goes below spanning the full width - never duplicated per panel.

exemplars.why_chosen: Double-column (a) naive / (b) fixed pair where a red cross marks the failure in (a).
exemplars.what_to_learn: Give both panels identical internal geometry and change exactly one thing; a red cross on the broken element is the whole argument.

exemplars.why_chosen: Two rows sharing one horizontal time axis, with a green 'Minimized Downtime' annotation on the gap being compared.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Two stacked timelines on one shared axis make a duration claim readable at a glance; keep role colours (stayer/leaver/joiner) identical across rows.

exemplars.why_chosen: Stacked (not side-by-side) comparison joined by an explicit 'V.S.' divider, with a dashed bracket naming the paper's scope.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Stack the two designs vertically when each is wide; a centred 'V.S.' label plus a dashed 'focus of this paper' bracket replaces sub-captions.

exemplars.why_chosen: Two mirrored mode panels bridged by a single central block that names the thing that changes.
exemplars.what_to_learn: For mode/state comparisons, put the transition operator physically between the panels rather than beside them.

exemplars.why_chosen: Double-column stacked panels where a numbered pipeline is defined once in (a) and reused inside two loops in (b).
exemplars.what_to_learn: Define a numbered sub-pipeline in the first panel, then reuse the same numbers inside the second panel's loops instead of renumbering.

exemplars.why_chosen: '(a) Now: Library+Sidecar' vs '(b) Our Vision' with an inside legend and per-panel operation traces that can be counted.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Naming the panels by claim rather than by system, and adding a countable trace strip under each, turns a structural comparison into a quantitative one.

exemplars.why_chosen: Flat (nesting 1) side-by-side comparison with a right-hand legend decoding box fill as operator type/state.
exemplars.what_to_learn: When box fill encodes state rather than identity, the legend belongs in a right-hand column and the panels stay pure grid.

exemplars.why_chosen: Panel (a)'s 7-component schematic (QPU array through bus and queue to shared QRAM) is paired with panel (b)'s Big-O table, the schematic-plus-cost-table two-panel variant, at high confidence with only 3 flows.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Use a metrics table, not a second schematic, as panel (b) when the comparison is quantitative: rows are the metrics, columns are the two designs, and Big-O terms substitute for exact numbers.

exemplars.why_chosen: A star exemplar of the frameless two-panel variant: colour alone (green Offline Stage, blue Online Execution) divides the two halves, packing 15 components and 13 flows, well above the template's median of 11 and 5.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Skip the dividing rule: give each stage its own fill colour (green offline, blue online) so the two-panel split reads from colour alone, and use dashed arrows only for the feedback edges (Kernel Info back to the Profiler).

exemplars.why_chosen: Two machine panels share one inside legend (blue/orange/gray proclet types) at the top, with per-machine CPU/RAM bars and a warning icon making the resource-pressure asymmetry that motivates the arrows immediately visible.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Put one shared legend above both panels, not one per panel, then reuse its colours in a small utilization-bar readout under each panel; mark the trigger condition (a red warning triangle on the strained resource) so the dashed migrate/split/merge arrows have a visible cause.

exemplars.why_chosen: Two dashed-outline containers (Load Balancer, LLM Replicas) stand in for panel frames, each internally nested three levels deep, connected by two labelled cross-panel arrows (Requests, Migration) that state exactly what crosses the boundary.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Use a dashed rounded outline as a lightweight panel boundary instead of a hard frame, and always label the arrows that cross between panels with the noun they carry (Requests, Migration) rather than leaving the connective implicit.

exemplars.why_chosen: The floor case for two-panel: just 6 components and 2 flows, monochrome except two red latency numbers (10-100ns vs 250-2000ns), proving a single colour contrast can carry the entire argument.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Keep both panels identical in structure (CPU/cache stack over memory) and spend your only colour on the one number that changes: the access latency in red beside the arrow it labels.

exemplars.why_chosen: Two labelled sub-figures (a)/(b) share one time-axis convention and bracket-arrow style to define four latency metrics (BCT, SCT, TTFT, TPOT), showing how a two-panel figure can do definitional work rather than just showing structure.
exemplars.what_to_learn: For a metric-definition figure, draw one shared time axis and mark each interval with a double-headed bracket labelled by its acronym, keeping the two panels' visual grammar (grid squares for done work, light shading for elapsed time) identical.

exemplars.why_chosen: A star, sparse-text exemplar of identical internal geometry across (a)/(b): the same stacked-card graph-index drawing convention and blue/red/gray search-path colour code repeat in both panels so only the storage tier differs.
exemplars.what_to_learn: When comparing two prior designs, redraw the same graph-index glyph and the same colour code (blue = visited path, red = top-k result, gray = unvisited) in each panel, changing only the storage medium each graph sits on.

exemplars.why_chosen: Stacked (not side-by-side) two-panel: an abstract matrix row-split on top and its concrete fork-join execution graph below share one orange-NPU/blue-GPU colour code end to end, at 13 components and 9 flows.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Stack an abstract data-partition diagram above the concrete execution graph it produces, and carry one colour pair (orange/blue) through both so a reader can trace the same partition from the matrix down into the parallel sub-graphs.

exemplars.why_chosen: A star exemplar of the plain dashed-divider variant (panels=1): Application Layer and Dynamic Layer sit either side of one vertical dashed rule, with red/green lines giving RX/TX its own small inside legend.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Divide the canvas with one plain vertical dashed rule instead of two boxed panels, bold the two side titles above it, and reserve colour (red RX, green TX) for the one distinction the case study is about.

exemplars.why_chosen: A star exemplar showing panel (b) built from labelled brackets over shared channel boxes rather than a redrawn schematic: yellow fill flags the hardware-isolated vSSDs against the software-isolated pair for a direct utilization-vs-isolation contrast.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Label the two conditions with brackets above the shared boxes (Software-isolated / Hardware-isolated) instead of duplicating structure, but do add a legend line for the highlight colour: this exemplar's own weakness is leaving that yellow-vs-plain fill unexplained.

exemplars.why_chosen: Sender and Receiver repeat identical box labels (Processor Core, Program Code, Local Apic) across a system bus, with numbered steps 1-7 tracing one interrupt end to end across both sides.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Overlay a single numbered path (1-7) across two mirrored panels to narrate one operation end to end, but label which side is which prominently: this exemplar's identical Processor Core/Program Code/Local Apic labels on both sides force readers back to the Sender/Receiver headers.

exemplars.why_chosen: Pairs one fully expanded MoE Block on the left with a tiled timeline of the same block repeated on the right, contrasting a one-shot Prefill pass against per-token Decoding steps at dense text density.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Expand the repeated unit once on one side (the MoE Block's internals) and tile the collapsed version across a timeline on the other side, so structure and repetition-over-time each get their own half instead of competing in one drawing.

exemplars.why_chosen: A star analogy exemplar: panel (a)'s software row/column access and panel (b)'s hardware ADE/IDE grid share matching green highlights on one row (R0) and column (C0), making the mapping visible.
exemplars.what_to_learn: To map a software concept onto hardware, draw matching panels and colour-highlight the same instance (one row, one column) in both; label the two access dimensions on the hardware grid's axes. Add a numbered connector between panels: this exemplar leaves that link to the caption.

exemplars.why_chosen: A star before/after exemplar: panel (a) frameworks split the loop (red, on the CPU) from MatMul/Add/Relu kernels on the accelerator, panel (b) fuses both into colour-matched Loop-uTasks mapped onto L0/L1/L2 hardware tiers.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Keep the same operator colours (blue MatMul, yellow Relu, gray Add) in both panels so a reader tracks exactly which pieces move from the CPU-side loop into accelerator-resident tasks; note panel (b)'s extra L0/L1/L2 tiers cost effort to map back to (a).

exemplars.why_chosen: This is the named overview-plus-zoomed-detail two-panel variant: nested DP/PP/Layer boxes on the left, with a dashed callout zooming one pipeline stage into CP/TP sublayers on the right, 20 components at nesting depth 3.
exemplars.what_to_learn: When one panel is a zoomed slice of the other rather than a comparable structure, connect them with a single dashed callout instead of forcing a second full panel frame; watch the font size once nesting reaches DP/PP/Layer/CP/TP depth, since this exemplar's own weakness is text too small for its nested detail.

exemplars.why_chosen: Three coloured path overlays over a repeated protocol-stack lane, with the legend below spelling out each path.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Overlay alternative paths in different colours on one shared substrate rather than drawing the substrate twice; the legend below then reads as a path list.

exemplars.why_chosen: The corpus's clearest flow-type legend: a 'Legends' block naming inter-device data (black solid), intra-device data (blue solid) and control (orange dashed).
exemplars.what_to_learn: Name every arrow class explicitly in an in-figure legend; three classes is the practical maximum and dashed should be reserved for control.

exemplars.why_chosen: Three tinted regions (Input / Optimizer / Training Runtime) wired by circled numbers 1-6 with a hardware row at the bottom.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Tinted dashed regions name the planes, circled numbers order the loop, and a plain device row anchors the bottom - all at single-column width.

exemplars.why_chosen: Numbered end-to-end flow over a control/data box layout in which exactly one of the repeated nodes is recoloured red-dashed.
exemplars.what_to_learn: To show a failure or special case among N identical elements, restyle one instance (red dashed) instead of adding a callout.

exemplars.why_chosen: Dispatcher to typed queues to typed engines with the control plane drawn as a separate box feeding back beneath the data path.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Draw the control plane as its own box under the data path with its own arrows, so 'who decides' is separable from 'what moves'.

exemplars.why_chosen: The most abstract control/data split in the corpus: a dashed horizontal divider with 'control plane' and 'data plane' as margin labels.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Borrow switch terminology literally - label the margins 'control plane' / 'data plane' and let the divider do all the grouping work. (No PDF-extracted print.png; this is a TeX-only figure.)

exemplars.why_chosen: Two named horizontal bands bridged by an identically labelled 'Communication Interface' in each, with two colour-coded channels.
exemplars.what_to_learn: When two subsystems talk over a channel, draw the same interface box in both bands - the repeated label is what makes the boundary legible.

exemplars.why_chosen: Double-column control-data figure with a top-left legend defining both colour and arrow semantics plus 8 circled steps.
exemplars.what_to_learn: At double column there is room for a full legend block that defines module colours and arrow line styles together; put it in the top-left corner before the flow starts.

exemplars.why_chosen: Clean 7-component, 4-flow control/data split: an FPGA data plane with four SA Control Threads fans dashed lines into a single control-plane box stacking exactly three named components, avoiding a legend entirely.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Stack the control plane's three components vertically in one box, label each with its paper section number instead of a legend, and fan dashed lines from every data-plane unit into that shared box rather than drawing one arrow per component.

exemplars.why_chosen: Overlays two named flow classes, black I/O Flow and blue Scheduling Flow, on the same Main Core/Worker Core boxes, with an inside top legend and circled steps 1-3 numbering only the control arrows.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Put the two-arrow-color legend and polling-icon key in one top-left inside block, then number only the control-flow arrows (steps 1-3) while leaving the data arrows unnumbered so the eye separates what happens always from what the scheduler decides.

exemplars.why_chosen: Names its two planes directly in the boxes (Valinor-H Data-plane inside the kernel stack, Valinor-H Control-plane outside it) and hands off through explicit Write/Read arrows into a shared per-CPU ring buffer across 20 components.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Label the two planes inline where they sit in an existing OS stack rather than boxing them separately, and embed a short struct snippet to document the wire format crossing the ring buffer; draw one explicit arrow from the hook point to the control plane instead of relying on adjacency.

exemplars.why_chosen: Star-rated, high-confidence 5-component figure that separates a solid data path (direct read/write to a shared Object) from a dashed control path (createObject/getObject calls) with an in-figure legend and five circled steps ordering the whole exchange.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Draw two symmetric peers around a shared object in the middle, label its access rights (WO/RO) directly on the box, and run the mediating monitor as a full-width band underneath; if you mark denied access with a red X, add it to the legend, unlike this figure.

exemplars.why_chosen: Star-rated: a dashed horizontal divider cleanly separates three data-plane pods above from a two-phase control plane below, with lettered (a)/(b)/(c) callouts tying each crossing arrow to body-text explanation instead of an in-figure legend.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Use one dashed rule as the entire plane boundary, then letter (not number) the arrows that cross it when their meaning needs the body text rather than a self-contained legend; color the two control-plane phases (orange pre-profiling, green slowdown) so their converging arrows read as one pipeline.

exemplars.why_chosen: Star-rated fast/slow-path variant: instead of two boxed planes, bold red Slow-Path and green Fast-Path bars sit beneath the shared Linux Driver, so color alone, not dashing, separates control-path IPC calls from the data-path IRQ.
exemplars.what_to_learn: When two paths share the same component, skip separate plane boxes and instead run a colored bar (red control, green data) directly under the shared box, with circled numbers 1-4 tracing the single request across both paths.

exemplars.why_chosen: Textbook top/bottom split: four numbered steps trace the operator's preference-tuning control loop above one dashed rule, while the critical path below runs jobs into a color-tiered Weighted-Fair-Queuing table with no legend needed.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Stack the slow control loop above a single dashed divider and the fast critical path below it; number only the control loop's steps (1-4) since that is what the operator actually walks through, and let color tiers in the resource table stand in for a legend.

exemplars.why_chosen: 14-component figure legends three devices below (dashed red = control via shmem, solid arrow = data, square = relay buffer) and reuses one blue hue across two GPUs to show a borrowed relay path.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Put the flow-class legend below the figure with icons for line style and shape (dashed=control, solid=data, square=buffer), and reuse one arrow color across two destinations when a worker's data can land in either place; but unlike here, also legend what each color itself means.

exemplars.why_chosen: Densest figure in the batch (14 components, nesting depth 3, star-rated): two separate inside legends, one for chunk state and one for solid/dashed-red flow type, sit top-left above N replicated inference instances.
exemplars.what_to_learn: When one figure needs two kinds of legend, state (chunk fill/hatch) and flow type (solid vs dashed-red arrows), keep both inside the frame but in separate corners rather than merging them, and let the replicated instances below use a plain ellipsis so the control components above stay the visual anchor.

exemplars.why_chosen: Minimal control-data instance: only 7 components and 2 flows separate one small Index/Client control box (top-right) from a dashed Memory-Node group whose ellipsis-joined pair forms the actual replicated data plane.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Group the replicated data-plane nodes in one dashed box separate from the small control-plane index/client pair, and use only two nodes plus an ellipsis rather than drawing every replica; avoid this figure's mistake of setting labels in a small serif font that hurts legibility.

exemplars.why_chosen: Star-rated: an offset stack of Pod 0/1/N cards (replication) sits inside a dashed Data-Plane box, wired by a bottom legend's orange data-flow and blue control-flow arrows to a separate dashed Control-Plane box.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Box the data plane and control plane as two separate dashed regions, use an offset card stack (Pod 0/1/N) to show replication inside the data-plane box without drawing every pod, and put a two-color arrow legend below to name data flow versus control flow.

exemplars.why_chosen: Star-rated two-tier control figure (19 components, nesting depth 4): a Cluster tier predicts and schedules above a Server tier, whose Oversubscription Agent manages a segmented memory bar mapping colored bands to concrete example VMs.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Stack a cluster-level control tier above a per-server agent tier inside two dashed regions, and instead of a separate legend, resolve the color coding by mapping each memory band directly to a named example VM (GPVM1, CoachVM2) below; label bands in the box itself since this figure's colors are not otherwise legended.

exemplars.why_chosen: Dense 15-component figure whose bottom legend spells out six path types (Tx/Rx control, Tx/Rx data, host data, auxiliary), all converging on one mandatory Attestation-kernel choke point between PCIe DMA and the RoCE protocol kernel.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Draw a security module as a literal inline choke point on both Tx and Rx paths, not a side box, so nothing bypasses it; this figure legends six path classes below, more than the template's usual three-class cap, so only go that far if every class needs its own arrow style.

exemplars.why_chosen: A microarchitecture reverse-engineering variant: circled steps 1-4 trace an enable-select-predict-update control loop through a 256-entry counter table, with two dashed 'Uncovered'/'Not fully studied' boxes marking the control logic this paper newly exposes.
exemplars.what_to_learn: When the control logic itself is the paper's discovery, dash-box exactly the parts labeled uncovered or not fully studied rather than a generic control-plane region, and walk the reader through the mechanism with circled steps overlaid on a decision-diamond flowchart plus one highlighted table row as a worked example.

exemplars.why_chosen: Star-rated triangular control loop: three subsystem boxes, each tagged with its paper section number, are joined by red arrows individually labeled with the action carried (Latency, Update, Plan, Compute) instead of a generic legend.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Name each control arrow with the verb it performs (Latency, Update, Plan, Compute) instead of a bare control/data label, tag each subsystem box with its own paper section number, and keep a tiny inline legend only for the one sub-panel (the timeline) that needs its own notation.

exemplars.why_chosen: Smallest hub-spoke here (5 components): a global controller fanning dotted control lines over an application graph, with one node magnified.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Dotted curved lines are the right weight for 'the hub controls all of these'; magnify exactly one spoke to show what a controlled node contains.

exemplars.why_chosen: The canonical scheduler-to-N-workers figure: one hub on the left, Worker 0 / Worker 1 / ... / Worker N-1 stacked on the right.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Draw the first two spokes in full, then an ellipsis row, then the last one labelled N-1; never draw more than three concrete replicas.

exemplars.why_chosen: Double-column (aspect 4.12), the widest clean hub-spoke: control subsystem, then a coloured heterogeneous topology, then a per-node zoom.
exemplars.what_to_learn: At double column a hub-spoke becomes three left-to-right zones (controller / topology / one-node detail) with the legend below.

exemplars.why_chosen: (a) a 4x4 fully connected chip mesh, (b) one chip enlarged - topology and node internals in one figure.
exemplars.what_to_learn: For mesh/topology figures, panel (a) is the graph and panel (b) is a dashed-connected zoom of a single node; the shared HBM bar spans the bottom of (b).

exemplars.why_chosen: Controller hub wired to three peer servers each showing the same GPU/DRAM/SSD tier stack, with lettered placement markers.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Give every spoke an identical internal template and vary only its contents; letters (A, B) then annotate which spoke holds what.

exemplars.why_chosen: Numbered client-to-scheduler-to-replicas walkthrough with an inside legend for allocated vs unallocated GPU icons.
exemplars.what_to_learn: When resource state is encoded by icon fill, the legend must define the icon, not the box; a right-hand brace can then annotate 'one kernel = 3 replicas'.

exemplars.why_chosen: Clients cloud fanning into a primary and two backups, with an inside legend for GET vs PUT/DEL and a small configuration table.
exemplars.what_to_learn: A replicated-store figure needs three things: a client source, one expanded server, and collapsed peers; the legend distinguishes operation classes by line style.

exemplars.why_chosen: Two-level global/local scheduler hierarchy with a right-hand legend separating migration control (orange solid) from other control (dashed).
exemplars.what_to_learn: One expanded instance beside two schematic ones communicates scale-out; the legend then only has to explain the one arrow class that matters.

exemplars.why_chosen: A high-ranked hub-spoke that closes into a loop: Cilantro Scheduler is the hub, Job 1/Job 2/... in the Shared Cluster are interchangeable spokes, and feedback/allocation arrows form a full cycle rather than one-way dispatch.
exemplars.what_to_learn: A hub can both dispatch to and learn from its spokes: draw the return arrow (Per-Job Feedback) the same weight as the dispatch arrow (Resource Allocations) and label each with the concrete payload it carries, not with a generic loop.

exemplars.why_chosen: A star example: a dashed allocator hub on top with two colour-coded resource pools, bold red Control Path arrows fanning down to Host 1 ... Host N spokes sharing one identical internal template.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Give the hub a dashed boundary and colour its internal resource pools by type (orange SSD, teal NIC), then draw only Host 1 and Host N with an ellipsis between, each an identical Instance-plus-Engine box, and put the fan-out arrows in one bold accent colour.

exemplars.why_chosen: A star exemplar of the shared-band variant: three identical vSSD/RL-agent columns (yellow outer box, monitor plus model) each exchange Actions/Reward with one Admission Control band below rather than radiating around a single hub.
exemplars.what_to_learn: When N identical agents all talk to one shared coordinator, it can sit below them as a horizontal band instead of beside them as a box; keep every agent column visually identical and mark its two channels (Actions up, Reward down) the same way in each.

exemplars.why_chosen: Request Scheduler is drawn centrally as the hub with cache-hit/cache-miss queues fanning below it into a shared GPU worker pool, while a side Global Monitor closes a separate feedback loop into the same hub.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Route both the main dispatch path and a side monitoring loop through the same central hub, but budget more space around it than this exemplar does: its weakness is that many small labelled arrows crowd the scheduler and make the routing logic dense to trace.

exemplars.why_chosen: TreeVQA Controller is a dashed hub box holding stacked-card spokes C_i/C_k/C_j; a thin connector drops one spoke (C_j) down into a magnified detail panel showing its optimize/split decision loop.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Draw spokes as small stacked cards, a shorthand for identical parallel instances, inside a dashed hub boundary, then pick exactly one spoke and connect it with thin lines to a magnified panel below that spells out its internal decision logic with a Yes/No diamond.

exemplars.why_chosen: The switch is the hub with two deliberately asymmetric spokes, an NF-compute server handling headers and an RDMA-memory server handling payloads, each returning results the switch's rebuilder reassembles in order.
exemplars.what_to_learn: A hub's spokes need not be identical: when two offload targets do genuinely different jobs, still draw them as parallel boxes at the same level, and colour-code the shared unit that threads through both, four packet flows here, so the reader can follow one flow out to its spoke and back.

exemplars.why_chosen: A textbook hub-spoke: Conveyor Core's shared database sits at the centre with circled steps 1-7 radiating out to Release Creator, Run Scheduler and Run Manager, plus two dashed pluggable-service groups as sub-spokes.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Number every arrow touching the hub in one continuous sequence (1-7) so a reader can replay one full request cycle through a database-centred hub, and group interchangeable plug-ins (Artifact Finders, Action Services) in a dashed box; this exemplar's own weakness is skipping a legend for its dashed-vs-solid convention.

exemplars.why_chosen: A star exemplar that annotates each mechanism with its paper section number (section 5, 6.1, 6.3) on the diagram itself, with Frontend as hub fanning into GPU group 0 ... GPU group n spokes.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Tie each drawn mechanism to its paper section number right on the box, so the figure doubles as a reading index; but name what the ellipsis between group 0 and group n hides, since leaving it uncounted is this exemplar's own recorded weakness.

exemplars.why_chosen: At exactly 29 components, the hub-spoke ceiling the template guide itself warns about, where a top telemetry band and VM Allocator hub feed a physically nested aisle/row/instance hierarchy that multi-tier could equally claim.
exemplars.what_to_learn: At this scale, reserve one accent colour (red) purely for the paper's new contribution, here the two highlighted Instance Configurator boxes and their routing path, so the one novel mechanism stays findable inside 600 shapes and 72 text boxes of otherwise uniform infrastructure.

exemplars.why_chosen: The broker is one large box literally straddling two symmetric Cloud A / Cloud B backends below, at medium confidence, illustrating hub-spoke's coordinator-over-peers idea with dashed catalog-feed lines distinct from the solid job-spec arrow.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Use a lighter dashed line for background catalog/status traffic into the hub and a solid line for the actual job request. This exemplar's weakness: with only two named clouds and no ellipsis, it does not visually confirm the broker scales beyond a pair.

exemplars.why_chosen: Reassigned from hub-spoke by the note-writer: one controller box with three distinct, non-identical neighbours (an external interface above, a data interface beside, an agent below) is flanked-core's engine-between-bands shape, not a hub with interchangeable peer spokes.
exemplars.what_to_learn: The real lesson is flanked-core's, not hub-spoke's: place the external caller interface above the engine, the executing agent below it, and a second interface beside it, then colour the engine's internal function-dispatch modules (orange) distinctly from its boundary (blue).

exemplars.why_chosen: A numbered star exemplar: circled steps 0-7 trace one query from client through the Router hub's EDF queue and scheduler out to two colour-coded Worker spokes, with an inset heatmap explaining the offline profiler.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Run one continuous numbered path (0-7) from client through the hub's internal EDF queue, scheduler and dispatcher out to the workers and back, and let two colour-coded example queries (green, blue) walk the same numbered path to different spokes to show scheduling in action, not just structure.

exemplars.why_chosen: The minimal N=2 case: an Edge PoP hub splits traffic exactly 50/50 into two identical Region spokes, each an identical Zone1/Stateful pair, with a bidirectional replication arrow standing in for the hub-spoke return path.
exemplars.what_to_learn: When there are genuinely only two spokes, skip the ellipsis and draw both in full, identically; a single yellow box can flag a special-case zone, but this exemplar's weakness is not legending what that highlight colour means.

exemplars.why_chosen: The AFC Server is the hub: a 2x3 grid packs six named functions into one box, flanked by a client access point on one side and two distinct NRA databases as spokes on the other.
exemplars.what_to_learn: When a hub's real content is a set of named functions rather than repeated workers, lay them out as a small labelled grid inside the hub box, but add a legend or colour convention separating request/response traffic from the database-feed arrows, since this exemplar leaves both unlabelled by anything but position.

exemplars.why_chosen: One central PEFT-as-a-Service Interface bar is the hub for three peer subsystem boxes below it, and every arrow to and from the hub is labelled with the exact payload (PEFT model, requests, responses) it carries.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Draw the hub as a thin horizontal bar rather than a box when its whole job is mediating traffic, and label every bidirectional arrow with the noun it exchanges in each direction, not just an arrowhead; keep the layout tight since this exemplar's weakness is a dense, icon-packed square.

exemplars.why_chosen: A numbered, dual-workflow hub-spoke where colour distinguishes download from distribution steps, though the record itself flags the Client-to-HyperEdge-Device shortcut arrow as breaking a clean hub-and-spoke shape.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Overlay two workflows on one architecture with a two-line colour legend (blue download, orange distribution) reusing the same three boxes for both; this exemplar's own weakness is a direct Client-Device link that bypasses the Tracker hub, and numbering that restarts per workflow.

exemplars.why_chosen: Reassigned from hub-spoke by the note-writer: this is a nested-containment deployment diagram, AWS containing continent containing region, not a coordinator with fanning spokes; the record itself calls it a nested containment diagram.
exemplars.what_to_learn: The transferable move is nested-stack's, not hub-spoke's: colour each containment level a different dashed hue (orange AWS, gray continent, green region) so the geographic scope reads at a glance, then attach the small node-type boxes (Clients, Brokers, Servers) with plain bidirectional arrows inside the innermost box.

exemplars.why_chosen: Reassigned from hub-spoke by the note-writer: this is a 4-component trust-dependency mesh (Microvium depends directly on all three of Switcher, Allocator and Scheduler) with no single coordinator, closer to dataflow-dag than to hub-spoke.
exemplars.what_to_learn: The transferable lesson is a small trust/dependency graph, not hub-spoke: colour each node by its one narrow privilege, number each node to a legend entry below stating exactly what it is trusted for, and let a non-trusted example component (Microvium) hang off the graph to show what depending on the TCB looks like.

exemplars.why_chosen: Already flagged low-confidence: three pink AQUA-* control components sit around a stacked multi-server NVLink Domain, but the record's own note that the source text was truncated before explaining their roles limits how much this teaches.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Stack repeated resource-pool sheets to suggest the design generalizes across many servers, and single out one concrete instance (GPU 8, in dark magenta) inside the schematic pool; but do not leave any arrow's meaning to inference, as this exemplar does with its two unexplained dashed GPU-to-GPU links.

exemplars.why_chosen: Reassigned from hub-spoke by the note-writer: three successively magnified panels, wafer to die to core, is overview-with-inset's own named 3-level chained (a)-(b)-(c) sequence, not a hub dispatching to interchangeable spokes.
exemplars.what_to_learn: For a hardware hierarchy with 3+ magnification levels, chain (a)(b)(c) panels left to right instead of one hub-spoke drawing, carry one highlight device across the boundary (the red X marking a bypassed core in (b), traced to a blue-outlined core in (c)), and let the mesh inside one panel, not radiating spokes, show replication.

exemplars.why_chosen: Six-panel grid (a)-(f) with a shared six-entry legend below, and a dashed box grouping (b)-(e) as the expansion of (a).
exemplars.what_to_learn: A dashed box around a sub-grid says 'these panels expand that panel'; the shared legend below is defined once for all six. Note: the PDF-extracted print.png includes a line of surrounding body text; use preview.png for the clean figure.

exemplars.why_chosen: (a)/(b) baselines drawn small next to a larger, more detailed (c) proposal, using one node vocabulary throughout.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Panel size is an argument: keep baselines schematic and give the contribution the detail budget.

exemplars.why_chosen: Pure cell-grid figure (6 components, 0 flows) with the legend inside above the grid and a highlighted cell in the summary table.
exemplars.what_to_learn: A matrix can have zero arrows: cells carry the state, the legend above defines cell colours, and one highlighted cell carries the point.

exemplars.why_chosen: Three rows - Baseline / Prior Work / This Work - each an identical prompt-to-image mini-pipeline, with the bottom row on a shaded ground.
exemplars.what_to_learn: The row-per-approach matrix: same left-to-right skeleton per row, dashed row separators, and a shaded background on the row that is yours.

exemplars.why_chosen: Three-column taxonomy (Type / Issues / Diagnosis) with percentages and colour carried consistently across columns.
exemplars.what_to_learn: For a measurement taxonomy, use column headers as the schema and keep row colour constant across columns so categories track visually.

exemplars.why_chosen: Double-column three-panel hardware comparison (aspect 4.84) with a shared right-hand numbered legend and 0 weaknesses.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Give the panel you actually care about more width than its baselines, and put the shared path numbering in a right-hand legend column reused by the whole paper.

exemplars.why_chosen: Small multiples: three model stacks side by side annotated with the same check/cross vocabulary at every layer boundary.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Small multiples work when the annotation vocabulary is fixed across panels; the reader compares mark positions, not shapes.

exemplars.why_chosen: N repeated identical columns (pool 1 / pool 2 / pool N) feeding one shared horizontal band, nesting depth 3.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Column-per-instance over a full-width shared band is the layout for 'per-X mechanics feeding one global step'; the dashed band border marks where they merge.

exemplars.why_chosen: High-confidence matrix exemplar at floor size, 8 components and 6 flows, with the row-equals-layer, column-equals-core-replica grid drawn literally: three identical Core columns each stack Driver, Application and Monitoring bands feeding one shared Aggregator.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Draw each replica as one column and each shared concern as one row so both axes carry meaning, keep every column's internal band colours identical, and route many-to-one aggregation as curved arrows into a single box at the margin instead of drawing every core's own output stage.

exemplars.why_chosen: Star, high-confidence matrix exemplar cited in the template's variant list: a rank-by-rank grid with zero flows where green cells mark layers replicated across three ranks and orange cells mark the part unique to each rank.
exemplars.what_to_learn: When the point is which state is shared and which is per-instance, drop arrows entirely and let identical fill colour across a row say replicated while a distinct colour per row says unique per instance, repeating the same row layout in a second panel for a related kind of state.

exemplars.why_chosen: Reassigned from matrix by the note-writer: this is a hardware evaluation composite of five unlike panels, chip photo, zoomed photo, an area/power table, two waveform plots, not comparable cells, so it fits composite-figure or overview-with-inset better than matrix.
exemplars.what_to_learn: When bundling a chip photo, a zoomed detail, a results table and measured waveforms into one figure, treat it as an overview-plus-detail composite rather than forcing a matrix grid; the record's own weakness warns that packing five different panel types into one single-column figure makes every axis label too small to read.

exemplars.why_chosen: Star, high-confidence matrix exemplar of a design-space table: four stacked policy rows share the identical CPU-to-GPU column structure, with an inside legend defining buffer-location colours and solid-versus-dashed arrow meaning.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Stack design-space alternatives as rows sharing one identical column skeleton so only the boxes that differ stand out, and put a compact legend inside the frame when colour marks buffer location and line style marks timing; the record warns that reusing one generic label for different colours invites confusion.

exemplars.why_chosen: Star, high-confidence double-column matrix with 6 lettered panels sharing one legend on the right: a top row frames a connectivity gap with a bold red arrow and a bottom row compares two solution families.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Arrange a problem-then-solutions matrix as a top row stating the mismatch and a bottom row of lettered panels comparing candidate fixes, define component colours once in a shared legend at the right edge, and let one bold callout arrow, not a whole panel, carry the gap argument.

exemplars.why_chosen: High-confidence matrix exemplar whose grid element is one labelled panel, a worked RLP/TLP/Reschedule/RESULT decision table walking through the scheduler token by token, attached beside a system diagram and two internal zoom-in panels.
exemplars.what_to_learn: When a design-space matrix is only part of a larger figure, give it its own labelled panel with named row headers and step through one concrete worked example column by column, rather than describing the decision rule in prose.

exemplars.why_chosen: Star, high-confidence matrix exemplar reading as a physical resource map: identical Hybrid Compute Tile cells surround one central Front End, with a callout zooming from one grid cell into its stacked analog-over-digital internal structure.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Use a matrix of identical tile cells to depict physical placement of replicated hardware around one shared control block, and zoom from a single selected cell into an exploded detail panel rather than expanding every cell, keeping the grid itself uncluttered.

exemplars.why_chosen: High-confidence 2x2 matrix comparing four PEFT architectures against the same backbone pipeline, with one legend at the top shared across all four panels defining operator colour and reserved-versus-pruned arrow style.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Redraw the identical backbone pipeline in every cell and let only the small inserted operator boxes and the solid-versus-dashed activation arrows change between cells, with one shared legend above the whole grid rather than one per panel.

exemplars.why_chosen: High-confidence matrix exemplar of two mirrored page-table rows, a guest chain above and a shadow chain below, cross-linked column by column by vertical arrows, with a dashed rule separating read-write region from read-only one.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Line up two parallel same-depth chains, real versus shadow or baseline versus protected, as two rows sharing identical column headers, and connect them with one vertical arrow per column instead of a tangle of diagonal lines, using one dashed rule to mark which side is mutable.

exemplars.why_chosen: Star, high-confidence matrix exemplar combining a lettered 3-panel layout with one inside legend: one panel is a tile-array resource map, and leader lines carry one colour vocabulary from an annotated graph into a zoomed tile.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Use one consistent colour-and-shape legend across a graph panel, a physical tile-grid panel, and a zoomed detail panel so a single leader line walks the reader from an abstract motif to the exact hardware block executing it; keep leader lines from crossing an unrelated middle panel, a flaw the record flags here.

exemplars.why_chosen: Star, high-confidence matrix exemplar with a genuine 2-by-3 grid, two cases against three rounds, tracing coloured numbered arrows through identically laid-out cells, with a legend below defining buffer-segment and arrow colours.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Build the grid so every cell keeps the identical buffer sketch and only the highlighted arrow colour and an enable/disable label change between cells, and put the one legend below the whole grid rather than repeating it per cell; six dense cells plus a separate schematic is already a lot, so keep individual cells sparse.

exemplars.why_chosen: High-confidence matrix exemplar of small multiples: the same retrieval-head-to-LLM gather diagram is redrawn across four attention-mechanism panels, beside a pruned-architecture panel with two accompanying bar charts.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Repeat one gather diagram unchanged across attention-mechanism variants and change only the internal grouping step; the record flags that reusing pruned and selected colour coding across five panels without one shared legend is a real risk, so add the legend once even at this density.

exemplars.why_chosen: High-confidence matrix exemplar of four numbered Tenant/Host/NIC mini-stacks sharing one ownership-colour legend on the right, showing exactly which layer intercepts control verbs in each virtualization scheme.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Repeat the identical three-row stack across numbered variants and colour every box by a fixed ownership vocabulary so the eye compares roles, not shapes; the weakness here warns that without a visible border between variants, the layout can misread as one crowded panel instead of four.

exemplars.why_chosen: High-confidence matrix exemplar built as a 9-stage-by-4-app grid, far denser than this template's usual floor, where each app keeps one colour across its path line and the queue cells it touches.
exemplars.what_to_learn: When several items' paths overlap on some grid cells and diverge on others, give every item one consistent colour for both its route line and its cell icons; the weakness here warns this pattern breaks down once cell count passes a few hundred, so cap the grid before density hides the comparison.

exemplars.why_chosen: High-confidence matrix exemplar of six numbered self-contained panels read column by column, each a mini-diagram of one compiler stage, tied together by one shared node-colour legend and one running worked example.
exemplars.what_to_learn: When a pipeline has too many stages for one row, fold it into a numbered grid read column by column, and keep one running worked example visible in every cell; a legend placed only at the bottom is far from the panels that need it first, so place it near the top instead.

exemplars.why_chosen: Star, high-confidence matrix exemplar of a three-column analogy: two baseline systems and the proposed one share four row labels in a left gutter, with a dashed box standing for a structural absence, not a component.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Put the row categories once in a left-hand gutter shared by every column, use a dashed empty box to mean no interface exists here rather than omitting the cell, and recolour only the one column that is the paper's contribution to argue its analogy to an accepted precedent.

exemplars.why_chosen: High-confidence matrix exemplar of four invocation columns sharing identical invocation, effects, overlay-state and filesystem rows, with the final column greyed out to separate a commit phase from the three live invocations.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Repeat the same row categories down every example column, and grey out an entire column to mark a later, separate phase rather than drawing it as a different diagram; label small isolation-dimension tabs consistently across all columns.

exemplars.why_chosen: Star, medium-confidence matrix exemplar comparing three systems in three columns against shared row labels in a left gutter, with the contribution's column visibly simpler, one merged box instead of split caches.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Keep row labels in one left gutter shared by every column so structural simplification reads at a glance from box count alone; the record warns that a highlight colour used on only two small icons is easy to miss, so give an important cue more than a token-sized swatch.

exemplars.why_chosen: Medium-confidence matrix exemplar that indexes a dynamic-programming grid with small node-link graphs as its row and column headers, then overlays coloured arrows and text directly on cells to walk through each transition type.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Use miniature diagrams, not just text, as row and column headers when the axes are themselves structured objects, and annotate individual cells with a coloured arrow for each rule the table encodes rather than a separate explanation, ending on one highlighted result cell.

exemplars.why_chosen: Low-confidence, flawed matrix exemplar: four numbered panels repeat a layered stack split into Local/Remote columns to show where GPU disaggregation cuts the stack, but one panel breaks the two-column pattern the others share.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Repeat one layered stack across numbered panels and move only the Local/Remote boundary and its link type between panels; keep every panel's column structure identical, since dropping the split in just one panel, and never mapping fill colours to layer names elsewhere, breaks the comparison's consistency.

exemplars.why_chosen: Medium-confidence matrix exemplar of four lettered panels arranged left to right to show a historical progression, each a swimlane stack of privilege-mode rows, with one legend at the top shared by all four.
exemplars.what_to_learn: When variants show an evolution rather than a static comparison, order the lettered panels left to right to match that history, encode privilege or execution mode as horizontal lanes inside every panel, and keep the arrow-meaning legend at the top since it applies to every panel below it.

exemplars.why_chosen: Star, medium-confidence matrix exemplar of a 2x2 quadrant grid, each quadrant colour-coded and tied to one paper subsection number, read clockwise from the DNN model through plan-selection tradeoffs to generated device code.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Assign each quadrant of a 2x2 grid its own colour family and its own subsection number so the reading order is announced by the numbers rather than position alone; many similar pastel colours without a legend get hard to tell apart at this density, so keep quadrant palettes visibly distinct.

exemplars.why_chosen: Real-system side vs simulator side with a four-entry legend across the top encoding event type by arrow colour.
exemplars.what_to_learn: When the two sides exchange several kinds of event, encode the kind in arrow colour and put the legend above the whole figure.

exemplars.why_chosen: GPU / CPU / CXL-Mem boxes with circled numbers 1-3 that index a right-hand list rather than an arrow sequence.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Circled numbers can be an index into a legend list instead of a temporal order; say which by where the numbers point. (No PDF-extracted print.png; TeX-only figure.)

exemplars.why_chosen: Offline | Online split by a dashed vertical rule, with CPU and GPU sides, an icon legend on top and circled numbers 1-4.
exemplars.what_to_learn: One figure can carry two orthogonal splits (offline/online vertically, CPU/GPU horizontally) if each uses a different device: a dashed rule for one, lane labels for the other.

exemplars.why_chosen: Client | server with an inset that zooms the SSD internals, and 6 circled numbers spanning both levels.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Numbering may cross the zoom boundary: steps 1-6 run through both the top-level machines and the zoomed SSD, tying the levels together.

exemplars.why_chosen: The purest host-device stack: SmartNIC tiers on top, a PCIe MMIO/DMA band in the middle, host tiers mirrored below.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Mirror the two sides around a named interconnect band; the band is a full-width row, not an arrow.

exemplars.why_chosen: Three vertical lanes - Grace CPU | NVLINK-C2C (900GB/s) | Hopper GPU - with per-side optimisation boxes.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Give the interconnect its own lane and label it with its bandwidth; per-side contributions then sit in the lanes they belong to.

exemplars.why_chosen: The only double-column host-device figure in the corpus, with a right-hand legend for within-GPU (solid) vs via-PCIe (dashed) movement.
exemplars.what_to_learn: At double column, stack GPU memory over CPU memory on the left and run the numbered mechanism left-to-right across both.

exemplars.why_chosen: Star-rated three-box testbed variant: Compute Node, Switch, and Memory Node mirror the identical Network-Interface/PHY/SerDes tier stack, with the interconnect drawn as literal orange Ethernet cables into labeled P0/P1 ports rather than an abstract band.
exemplars.what_to_learn: When the interconnect is itself hardware worth showing, draw it as literal cabling with named ports (P0/P1) instead of a plain arrow, and mirror three color-coded node boxes (compute, switch, memory) with the same internal tier stack so the reader can compare them at a glance.

exemplars.why_chosen: Extreme size asymmetry: a small CPU/Controller pair broadcasts instructions into a large 3D grid of homogeneous vertex/edge PUs, with an inside dashed legend for the per-PU instruction/state/response cycle and a time axis beside the grid.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Let the two sides be wildly unequal in size when the paper's point is scale: a tiny controller box against a wall of identical device units, connected by fan-out (broadcast) and fan-in (convergecast) arrows, with a small dashed legend for the repeating per-unit cycle placed beside the small side.

exemplars.why_chosen: Double-column layout centers a literal circular free-list ring (Head/Tail, entries, null) inside the MN's Free MW Queue, with five circled steps and a dashed chain (MWTable to MW to Memory Chunk) crossing the CN/MN boundary.
